newsitem.title: ITALY: Milan airport chief wants changes to Linate transfer.
newsitem.headline: Milan airport chief wants changes to Linate transfer.

text.p: Giuseppe Bonomi, the new president of Societa Esercizi Aeroportuali Spa (SEA), managing company of Milan airports' system said he will immediately ask the Transport Minister, Claudio Burlando, to modify the decree ruling the transfer of acitivites from Linate to Malpensa.

Bonomi believes that Linate airport must maintain not only the Rome-Milan shuttle operations but also "strategic" links at the Milan-Paris and Milan-Frankfurt routes, not only for passenger services but for cargo transportation as well.

Earlier the general meeting of shareholders of Societa Esercizi Aeroportuali Spa (SEA), managing company of Milan airports' system, re-elected the administration board for the 1997-99 period. This in turn appointed Bonomi, a member of the Lega Nord parliamentary group, as SEA president and Alfredo Gianetti managing director and vice-president.

Other board members are Claudio Badocci, Guiseppe Bencini, Alberto Brambilla, Stefano Morri, Massimo Sordi, Carlo Tribuno (representing Milan Borough which holds 84,559 percent of shares) and Luciano Venturini (representing Milan Province which holds 14,558 percent of shares). - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
